findings.claim: PinnedBase's own docstring justifies its shape by invoking the exact incident it warns about ("this repo's history has an instance of adjacent same-typed parameters transposing and type-checking cleanly anyway"), and cites `check_readiness`'s keyword-only `*,` on `scratch`/`home` as the precedent being followed. But `PinnedBase` is declared `@dataclass(frozen=True)` with no `kw_only=True` and no `*` separator, so `mirror`, `url` and `base_sha` remain positionally constructible — and `url: str` and `base_sha: str` are themselves adjacent same-typed fields. A future `PinnedBase(mirror, base_sha, url)` call would type-check cleanly and silently swap the pinned base with the remote URL, reproducing precisely the class of bug the docstring says this design avoids; the one call site in this diff happens to use keywords, but nothing in the class enforces it the way `check_readiness` actually does.

No test asserts that `_batch_runner` actually receives `pinned.url` rather than some other `str` field on `PinnedBase` (e.g. `pinned.base_sha`) — every test that exercises this line either leaves `candidates` empty or mocks `run_batch`/`_batch_runner` before the `run()` closure that consumes `url` (in `_resolve_stacked_on` -> `package_phase.fetch_parent_branch`) ever executes. Since `url` and `base_sha` are both plain `str` fields, swapping `url=pinned.url` for `url=pinned.base_sha` at this line type-checks cleanly and leaves the full suite green (the call-count tests only prove `real_remote` isn't invoked a second time, not which pinned field was threaded through), so a transposition here — the exact class of bug `PinnedBase`'s own docstring is trying to guard against — would only surface in production, on a batch with an actual waiting stacked dependent.
